task: Write one sentence of your own using the word rudimentary. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know rudimentary should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Their heist plan was rudimentary — wear overalls, look bored, walk the painting out the front.
A simple tool is plain but complete — nothing missing, nothing extra; rudimentary means the development itself hasn't happened yet.
Skeletal goes past rudimentary — not underdeveloped but stripped to the bare frame, ribs with nothing on them.

Primitive points backward: an early, crude stage of something that has since advanced — a primitive engine, primitive surgery. Rudimentary needs no history; it says this thing, here and now, is basic and undeveloped for its purpose. A brand-new app can be rudimentary without ever being primitive.

Crude judges the workmanship: rough, unrefined, unfinished at the edges, whatever the stage of development. Rudimentary judges the development itself — the working shape exists and the growth has not happened yet. A crude thing was made roughly; a rudimentary one simply has not grown up.
far along in development
developed until even the fine points are handled

The flightless beetle still carries wings.
Under the shell lie two stubs a millimeter long, veined like the real thing, folded as if for a flight they will never take.
Naturalists call them rudimentary wings: the first shape of the thing, never finished — a sketch the species stopped drawing a hundred thousand generations ago.
Rudimentary is the exact word because the wings are basic and undeveloped — the beginnings of a thing, not the thing grown.
That's the word's center of gravity: a rudimentary skill, kit, or system has the working shape and none of the development.
It is not an insult; every finished thing was once a beginning.
It is simply a reading of how far from finished the thing stands.
Rudimentary measures development, not worth: a rudimentary skill or setup has the shape and awaits the growth.

Two neighbors to keep straight: elementary describes the ground floor itself — first-grade arithmetic is elementary and exactly as it should be — while rudimentary implies the thing is undergrown for its purpose.
And this unit's inept is harsher still: rudimentary skill is on its way; inept performance has arrived and failed.
